before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

steps.text: Fresh session per step: runner starts each step clean with a short handoff note from the progress file (session=new default)
Per-step model choice: Haiku/Sonnet for simple steps, Opus for hard ones; orchestrator suggests a model per step
Steps list exact files they need; session reads only those instead of exploring the repo
Trim tool output: cap long logs/command output before it returns to the model (configurable limits)
Shared registry: schema + store for headless session config (chain files, load mode, session mode, model rules, output caps, file scoping)
Shared registry: read/write API used by both Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio plugin, with change events so both stay in sync
Shared control components (usable in both plugins): CLAUDE.md chain view - every file in load order with size and token count
Shared controls: per-file include/exclude, load always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview
Shared controls: per-build and per-step chain overrides

before.title: Watchdog + watch-rule system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, everything)
before.detail: A server-side watchdog on the VPS that runs every few minutes, checks every orchestrator table (pending, queued, building, merge queue, UI Review) for rows whose build has already landed on main or is otherwise done, and removes or marks them complete automatically. Logs each cleanup and sends an FYI to AmberX.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I want a server fucking watchdog on the VPS to do that.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Design the stale-row contract stale-row@1 in framework/core/stale-rows.mjs: a pure classifier that takes a row (pending, queued, building, merge-queue entry, UI Review item) plus facts (PR merged on main, commits on main, build status complete/failed/cancelled, branch deleted, PR closed) and returns keep | complete | remove with a reason code. Add framework/schemas/stale-row.json for the cleanup log record (row kind, row id, build id, action, reason, evidence, at, by: watchdog)
steps.why: New cross-table contract and log schema that every orchestrator table and the console read

steps.text: Write fixture cases for the classifier (landed via merge queue, landed by direct merge commit, closed unmerged PR, build complete but row still queued, UI Review item whose PR merged, a running build that must stay, a missing-facts row that must stay) plus a check script
steps.why: Fixtures are the contract for the classifier

steps.text: Facts gatherer: framework/cli/stale-facts.mjs reads origin/main (git log --merges, branch heads) and the GitHub PR states through github-token.mjs with ETag caching, so a run costs almost no API calls; returns one facts map keyed by build id / branch / PR
Table readers for builds-store rows: pending, queued and building projections from _claude/builds/store.json via builds-store.mjs, each mapped to classifier input

Table readers for the merge queue (land.mjs queue list / merge-queue.mjs state) and UI Review items (review.mjs list), mapped to classifier input; reached through the capabilities, not folder names, where the framework calls them

Watchdog core apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog.mjs: run = gather facts, read every table, classify, and with --dry-run only print the plan; settings (enabled, interval minutes, dry-run, per-table on/off) in the plugin settings registry

Apply actions: builds store rows marked complete with the merged PR (builds-live.mjs so main sees it at once), merge-queue entries removed through land.mjs queue remove, UI Review items closed as merged; every write under the store lock and journalled, never touching a running build

Cleanup log: append each action as a stale-row@1 record to the plugin dataDir (watchdog/log.jsonl, rotated monthly) plus a build note on the affected build; also a Codebase changes log line per run that did anything

FYI to AmberX: one batched notification per run that cleaned something (count + row list), declared in the plugin's notify.json (notify-types@1) and sent through axf.notify@1 so the Notifications panel controls it
VPS schedule: cron axf-stale-watchdog every 5 minutes running watchdog.mjs run with a lockfile so runs never overlap; install/uninstall in the plugin's install.mjs / uninstall.mjs
Health check: register a health@1 check in the systems check (watchdog last run older than 3 intervals or last run failed = red banner item with Auto fix that reruns it / reinstalls the cron)

API: REST routes /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog (GET status + last runs + log, POST run, POST dry-run, PUT settings), MCP via plugin-commands (watchdog-status, watchdog-run, watchdog-log, watchdog-settings), CLI axf watchdog status|run|log|set, voice actions orchestrator.watchdog.*

UI: a Watchdog card in Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (settings, last run, Run now, Dry run) and a Cleanups log tab using framework controls and TabGroup; register console-control targets (view:…/tab:watchdog, setting:…) and console_show deep link

Tests: unit tests for table readers and apply actions against a temp store, merge-queue and UI Review fixtures (dry-run makes no writes, running builds untouched, second run is a no-op); wire check-stale-rows.mjs into CI

Run checks (check-stale-rows, watchdog tests, builds-store verify, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, glossary catalog --check), dry-run on the VPS data and paste its plan, UI Review submit with 3 options, write _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps.md, add the THREADS.md row, open the PR saying how REST/MCP/CLI/voice reach each part

Shared watch-rule engine on the VPS: rules = a pre-built thing to watch + conditions combined with AND / OR (with grouping) + a pre-built action, with values chosen from lists. Reusable by any screen; the stale-row cleanup becomes the first built-in rule.
Collapsible 'Watches' section on the Build orchestrator page listing its rules (expandable rows, on/off, last fired), with an 'Add watch' button.

'Add watch' wizard, zero typing: a grid of pre-built things to watch; selecting one expands the row to pick pre-built conditions and actions from lists and enter values (dropdowns, pickers, number steppers). Plain-English summary of the rule before saving.

AND / OR conditions per watch: '+ add condition' in the wizard, each joined by an AND/OR picker, plus condition groups (e.g. (A AND B) OR C) built by clicking, no typing; the plain-English summary shows the logic.
Same collapsible 'Watches' container with the Add-watch wizard on the Plan Studio page, with Plan Studio's own pre-built things to watch and actions.

A master collapsible 'All watches' container listing every possible thing that can be monitored across the system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, UI Review, merge queue, accounts, VPS, etc.), grouped by area, each addable with one click via the same wizard.

Gates tab in the Watchdog panel: lists every existing gate on the VPS (test gate on landing, UI Review gate, merge approval, budget caps, etc.) as expandable rows with on/off, what it blocks, last triggered; plus 'Add gate' using the same zero-typing wizard (pre-built things to check, AND/OR conditions, pre-built block/notify actions).

Health check: register a health@1 check in the systems check (watchdog last run older than 3 intervals or last run failed = red banner item with Auto fix that reruns it / reinstalls the cron)

API: REST routes /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog (GET status + last runs + log, POST run, POST dry-run, PUT settings), MCP via plugin-commands (watchdog-status, watchdog-run, watchdog-log, watchdog-settings), CLI axf watchdog status|run|log|set, voice actions orchestrator.watchdog.*

UI: a Watchdog card in Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (settings, last run, Run now, Dry run) and a Cleanups log tab using framework controls and TabGroup; register console-control targets (view:…/tab:watchdog, setting:…) and console_show deep link

Tests: unit tests for table readers and apply actions against a temp store, merge-queue and UI Review fixtures (dry-run makes no writes, running builds untouched, second run is a no-op); wire check-stale-rows.mjs into CI

Same collapsible 'Watches' container with the Add-watch wizard on the Plan Studio page, with Plan Studio's own pre-built things to watch and actions.

A master collapsible 'All watches' container listing every possible thing that can be monitored across the system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, UI Review, merge queue, accounts, VPS, etc.), grouped by area, each addable with one click via the same wizard.

Each tab: count in the tab label, expandable rows, on/off, and an Add button using the same zero-typing wizard.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

# Build: molly-native-expenses

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-08T16:58:59.537Z
> Standalone apps keep working until Molly covers them; list gaps as pending builds.

## What to build
Continue build "Molly gap: Expense Tracker screens load natively in Molly (Next.js 16 / React 19 app today)" (molly-native-expenses) [Molly] — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-08 16:58):
"Standalone apps keep working until Molly covers them; list gaps as pending builds."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/molly-native-expenses
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~?):
[x] s1 Expenses API reachable from molly.amberxai.com (CORS + session) without changing the standalone app
[ ] s2 Expenses ledger, paydays and reports as a Molly plugin on framework controls (shell-surface@1 manifest)
[ ] s3 Expenses assistant + settings as Molly plugin screens; menu entries in the all-apps index
[ ] s4 Tests, UI Review (3 options), report
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step molly-native-expenses <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link molly-native-expenses --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-5 (an API key: billed per token, keep it lean) for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step molly-native-expenses <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note molly-native-expenses "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

# Build: enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:43:57.553Z
> What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI.

## What to build
Continue build "Enforce the merge queue: every finished build goes into it and is batched into one combined build before CI" (enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:43):
"What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Enforce for all builds, no exceptions: when a build finishes it goes into the merge queue (never straight to main or its own CI run). The merge queue combines the queued builds into one batch build, resolves conflicts, then sends that single build to CI; on green it lands and redeploys. Reconcile with auto-land-every-build and the Batch Manager build. No AI for the queue logic. Full API control.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI.

before.title: Transparency token works on every dialog and settings window
before.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett: every surface must READ the glass/transparency token (wired in everywhere, always), even if it doesn't apply it. Whether a surface actually goes see-through is its own per-surface/per-instance switch (on/off), not missing wiring.

CORRECTION from Brett (replaces the previous note): NO on/off switch. Every surface reads its own transparency token value; the default value is 100% (fully opaque/visible). To make a surface see-through you lower its value. Per surface type tokens in tokens.style, overridable per instance (Quick settings).

before.title: Dispatcher gate: never launch a build that already has a live session
before.detail: Bug seen three times on Nov 13 (ui-manager-floating-window-to-select-any: Earl/Gina, Gina/Paulie, Lenny/Paulie): the orchestrator's dispatcher launched the same build phase twice on the same worktree, so two headless sessions wrote the same files at once. Also 'Self-check: marked running with no session' releases builds back to the Queue while a session is still alive. Fix: (1) a dispatch gate that refuses a launch while ANY live tmux/claude session exists for that build id or worktree (check tmux axf-<build>--*, claude -p pids and a lock file in the worktree); (2) the self-check must confirm a session is really dead (pid + tmux) before releasing; (3) a per-build lock file with heartbeat, where stale locks expire; (4) tests that simulate double dispatch. before.title: Watchdog + watch-rule system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, everything)
before.detail: A server-side watchdog on the VPS that runs every few minutes, checks every orchestrator table (pending, queued, building, merge queue, UI Review) for rows whose build has already landed on main or is otherwise done, and removes or marks them complete automatically. Logs each cleanup and sends an FYI to AmberX.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I want a server fucking watchdog on the VPS to do that.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Design the stale-row contract stale-row@1 in framework/core/stale-rows.mjs: a pure classifier that takes a row (pending, queued, building, merge-queue entry, UI Review item) plus facts (PR merged on main, commits on main, build status complete/failed/cancelled, branch deleted, PR closed) and returns keep | complete | remove with a reason code. Add framework/schemas/stale-row.json for the cleanup log record (row kind, row id, build id, action, reason, evidence, at, by: watchdog)
steps.why: New cross-table contract and log schema that every orchestrator table and the console read

steps.text: Write fixture cases for the classifier (landed via merge queue, landed by direct merge commit, closed unmerged PR, build complete but row still queued, UI Review item whose PR merged, a running build that must stay, a missing-facts row that must stay) plus a check script
steps.why: Fixtures are the contract for the classifier

steps.text: Facts gatherer: framework/cli/stale-facts.mjs reads origin/main (git log --merges, branch heads) and the GitHub PR states through github-token.mjs with ETag caching, so a run costs almost no API calls; returns one facts map keyed by build id / branch / PR
Table readers for builds-store rows: pending, queued and building projections from _claude/builds/store.json via builds-store.mjs, each mapped to classifier input

Table readers for the merge queue (land.mjs queue list / merge-queue.mjs state) and UI Review items (review.mjs list), mapped to classifier input; reached through the capabilities, not folder names, where the framework calls them

Watchdog core apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog.mjs: run = gather facts, read every table, classify, and with --dry-run only print the plan; settings (enabled, interval minutes, dry-run, per-table on/off) in the plugin settings registry

Apply actions: builds store rows marked complete with the merged PR (builds-live.mjs so main sees it at once), merge-queue entries removed through land.mjs queue remove, UI Review items closed as merged; every write under the store lock and journalled, never touching a running build

Cleanup log: append each action as a stale-row@1 record to the plugin dataDir (watchdog/log.jsonl, rotated monthly) plus a build note on the affected build; also a Codebase changes log line per run that did anything

FYI to AmberX: one batched notification per run that cleaned something (count + row list), declared in the plugin's notify.json (notify-types@1) and sent through axf.notify@1 so the Notifications panel controls it
VPS schedule: cron axf-stale-watchdog every 5 minutes running watchdog.mjs run with a lockfile so runs never overlap; install/uninstall in the plugin's install.mjs / uninstall.mjs
Health check: register a health@1 check in the systems check (watchdog last run older than 3 intervals or last run failed = red banner item with Auto fix that reruns it / reinstalls the cron)

API: REST routes /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog (GET status + last runs + log, POST run, POST dry-run, PUT settings), MCP via plugin-commands (watchdog-status, watchdog-run, watchdog-log, watchdog-settings), CLI axf watchdog status|run|log|set, voice actions orchestrator.watchdog.*

UI: a Watchdog card in Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (settings, last run, Run now, Dry run) and a Cleanups log tab using framework controls and TabGroup; register console-control targets (view:…/tab:watchdog, setting:…) and console_show deep link

Tests: unit tests for table readers and apply actions against a temp store, merge-queue and UI Review fixtures (dry-run makes no writes, running builds untouched, second run is a no-op); wire check-stale-rows.mjs into CI

Run checks (check-stale-rows, watchdog tests, builds-store verify, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, glossary catalog --check), dry-run on the VPS data and paste its plan, UI Review submit with 3 options, write _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps.md, add the THREADS.md row, open the PR saying how REST/MCP/CLI/voice reach each part

Shared watch-rule engine on the VPS: rules = a pre-built thing to watch + conditions combined with AND / OR (with grouping) + a pre-built action, with values chosen from lists. Reusable by any screen; the stale-row cleanup becomes the first built-in rule.
Collapsible 'Watches' section on the Build orchestrator page listing its rules (expandable rows, on/off, last fired), with an 'Add watch' button.

'Add watch' wizard, zero typing: a grid of pre-built things to watch; selecting one expands the row to pick pre-built conditions and actions from lists and enter values (dropdowns, pickers, number steppers). Plain-English summary of the rule before saving.

AND / OR conditions per watch: '+ add condition' in the wizard, each joined by an AND/OR picker, plus condition groups (e.g. (A AND B) OR C) built by clicking, no typing; the plain-English summary shows the logic.
Same collapsible 'Watches' container with the Add-watch wizard on the Plan Studio page, with Plan Studio's own pre-built things to watch and actions.

A master collapsible 'All watches' container listing every possible thing that can be monitored across the system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, UI Review, merge queue, accounts, VPS, etc.), grouped by area, each addable with one click via the same wizard.

Gates tab in the Watchdog panel: lists every existing gate on the VPS (test gate on landing, UI Review gate, merge approval, budget caps, etc.) as expandable rows with on/off, what it blocks, last triggered; plus 'Add gate' using the same zero-typing wizard (pre-built things to check, AND/OR conditions, pre-built block/notify actions).

Watchdog panel has exactly three tabs: 1) Watches (things being monitored + actions, incl. stale-row cleanup), 2) Gates (everything that blocks/holds work), 3) Rules (every standing rule the VPS enforces, e.g. account routing, auto-merge, rebuild-on-conflict, step splitting). Each tab: count in the tab label, expandable rows, on/off, and an Add button using the same zero-typing wizard.
